title: Poker Now Session Failure Rate
dataSources: BoardGameGeek plays (`bgg:play`), Poker Now sessions (`pokernow:session`), Bridge Base Online boards (`bridgebase:board`), and Lichess tournament rounds (`lichess:tournament`).
app: BoardGameGeek play logs, Poker Now session exports, Bridge Base Online boards, and Lichess tournament data ingested into Splunk.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=pokernow:session
| eval status_value=lower(coalesce(session_status,"unknown"))
| eval failed=if(match(status_value,"error|fail|alert|overdue|late|stale|breach"),1,0)
| stats count as events, sum(failed) as failed_events by table_name
| eval failure_pct=round(100*failed_events/events,1)
| sort - failure_pct - failed_events
description: Measures how often Poker Now session records land in an unhealthy or exception state for each table name.
value: A plain failure-rate view highlights noisy devices, flaky automations, and habits that repeatedly slip.
implementation: Normalize session_status values into good or bad states and review the failure percentage per table name.
visualization: Bar chart of failure percentage by entity.
grandmaExplanation: It highlights which parts of your Poker Now session data keep ending up in a bad state instead of working cleanly.
